headline: Third Rail, Third Attack: Ferrogate Lines Crippled Across Geartown Corridor
body:
A coordinated infrastructure strike disabled three Ferrogate Transit mainline segments early Tuesday morning, derailing a cargo shuttle near the Geartown depot and triggering tunnel collapses at junction points K-7 and K-11 in the Underworld network. No passenger trains were running at the time of the 03:14 detonation, but four Ferrogate maintenance workers were killed and eleven more are listed in critical condition at Helix Biosystems Trauma Unit 4. This marks the third major attack on Ferrogate infrastructure in 18 months, following the Narrows overpass bombing in March 2169 and the signal tower arson in the Gray Zone district last November.

Ferrogate Transit issued a statement confirming that 'externally placed thermite-composite charges' were responsible for the structural failures, and that Meridian Security Authority investigators are treating the incident as coordinated domestic terrorism. The company has suspended all freight operations on the eastern corridor indefinitely, a shutdown that analysts at Sterling Financial Digest estimate will cost 180,000 quanta per day in supply chain disruption. 'Geartown doesn't run without rail,' said Collective union rep Adaeze Miramoto-Park, who represents Ferrogate workers. 'Four of our people are dead. We're not calling this an inconvenience — we're calling it what it is.'

No group has formally claimed responsibility, though The Underground Signal broadcast an anonymous communiqué within hours of the attack praising the strike as 'a message written in steel.' Investigators have not confirmed any organizational link. Bore Rats, whose tunnel operations depend on Ferrogate corridor access, have publicly denied involvement and offered to assist with rescue recovery — an offer Ferrogate declined.
aftermath: Ferrogate announced a 600-million-quanta hardening program by year's end, contracting Ironclad to provide infrastructure security, a move that deepened existing tensions between Ironclad and The Collective.
runner_relevance: The Ferrogate shutdown created immediate demand for alternative freight movement, turning courier and smuggling contracts into a goldmine overnight — runners with Bore Rat contacts could charge triple rates for goods that normally traveled by rail. Ferrogate itself posted high-value protection contracts for repair crews working the damaged tunnels, and Ironclad hired runners as advance scouts to sweep junction points ahead of their own security teams. The Meridian Security Authority put out data-retrieval contracts seeking information on the bombers, while anti-corporate brokers were simultaneously paying for evidence of Ferrogate's alleged worker safety violations to use as deflection.
